name: Anglo-Saxonism
summary: Anglo-Saxonism is a 19th-century belief that the English-speaking peoples descend from Germanic stock and inherited from it free institutions, Protestantism and a talent for self-government. In its racial form it ranked Anglo-Saxons above other peoples and used that rank to justify empire, American continental expansion and a civilising mission, and some versions called for Anglo-American unity. It took no settled line on economics and little on social policy.
scope: The Victorian and Gilded Age racial strand in Britain and the United States: the Teutonic germ theory (Arnold, Stubbs, Freeman, Kingsley), Josiah Strong's Our Country, Roosevelt and Kipling on the English-speaking peoples' kinship and mission, and Anglo-American unity. Encyclopedia.com and Kramer describe a loose set of cultural assumptions from the 17th century that late-19th-century race theory made racial; this audit takes the racial form and leaves out the earlier non-racial tradition and later Nordicism.
